_what_is_measured: rho = r(leg B, POST-TRANSIENT) / r(leg A), both per-step CPU rates from ExecutionTime deltas WITHIN ONE RUN. Leg A: 40 steps, deltaT 0.02, t 0 -> 0.8 -- the window every C4/C5 wall factor was measured on, the donor's controlDict UNCHANGED. Leg B: 1110 steps, deltaT 0.1, startFrom latestTime, t 0.8 -> 111.8, of which the FIRST 40 ARE DISCARDED as the restart transient and the remaining 1070 are graded as two halves of 535. Leg B samples 12.4 % of the 900 s soak, against T25R6c's 4.4 %.
_why_1110_and_not_a_round_number: N_B IS DERIVED FROM T25R6c'S MEASURED TRAJECTORY, NOT CHOSEN. derive_t25R6cR2.py (committed, with its DESIGN_DERIVATION.json output) measures the post-transient window-rate scatter and finds it falls as a power law sd_pct(W) = exp(1.762373) x W^-0.186825 -- p = 0.187, NOT the 0.5 of independent noise, with lag-1 autocorrelation 0.273. Inverting it under the CONSERVATIVE assumption that the two halves are independent (the measured positive autocorrelation would only shrink the difference's sd and so SHORTEN leg B) gives the half length at which the UNCHANGED 5 % threshold sits at 1.96 sd of the measured drift: W_half = 531.5, rounded up to 535, so N_B = 40 + 2 x 535 = 1110 and the threshold sits at 1.9624 sd. Doubling leg B again would buy only 0.219 % off the per-half sd for double the compute; the return is flattening.
_the_predecessors_gate_was_unsatisfiable: THE HEADLINE OF THE DESIGN DERIVATION, AND IT IS THE REASON THE WINDOW CHANGED. T25R6c's statistic |r(last 40) - r(first 40)| / r(last 40) anchors `first` on leg-B steps 1-40, WHICH ARE THE RESTART TRANSIENT, measured 10.43 % CHEAPER (0.345750) than the settled level (0.386000). Extending leg B moves ONLY the `last` window, drawn from the settled distribution. The statistic therefore ASYMPTOTES TO 10.427 %, not to zero; passing at 5 % would need r(last 40) <= 0.363947 and ALL NINE observed post-transient 40-step windows exceed it (minimum 0.371250); the probability any given last-40 window falls below it is 2.5 %. THE DERIVED ANSWER TO 'HOW MANY LEG-B STEPS DRIVE IT TO 5 %' IS: NO FINITE COUNT. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT: with a 40-step window sd of 2.915 %, a perfectly FLAT leg B fails a 5 % endpoint gate about one time in five on noise alone. THE WINDOW WAS THE DEFECT, NOT THE THRESHOLD -- and the threshold NUMBER is carried into R2 UNCHANGED at 5 %.
_nothing_is_loosened_three_things_are_st: (1) THE WINDOW excludes the measured transient and splits the remainder in half -- the fix above. (2) THE NORMALISER: T25R6c divided by `last`, and with a RISING rate that is the SMALLER statistic -- its 13.939 % is 16.197 % under the other normaliser, SO ITS GATE FAILED UNDER THE LOOSER OF THE TWO AND WOULD ONLY HARDEN UNDER THE STRICTER, which makes that verdict robust to the choice. R2 removes the choice by computing BOTH and GRADING THE LARGER, registered in advance so nobody later 'tightens' the normaliser and mistakes a harder gate for a moved verdict. THIS IS NOT A D389 INSTANCE: D389 concerns normalising an ABSOLUTE TEMPERATURE by its mean, where the zero is arbitrary; a rate in s/step has a meaningful zero, so endpoint normalisation is legitimate here. D389 IS OPEN AND IS NOT SETTLED BY THIS RUNG. (3) rho IS GRADED ON THE POST-TRANSIENT WINDOW, which RAISES it from 1.063997 to a predicted 1.075209 and makes G-R2-2 HARDER, on a physical argument fixed before the run: the ladder runs 8,300 leg-B steps, so a 40-step transient is 0.48 % of the mixture and the settled rate is what prices the ladder. A NEW default-deny control C-R2-1 measures the run's OWN transient end and returns NOT A RESULT if it exceeds 40, so the 1.5x margin over the measured 26 is a CONTROL, not an assumption.
_the_write_defect_is_fixed_and_verified_: T25R6c graded NOT A RESULT partly because NO FIELD DIRECTORY EXISTED AT ITS REGISTERED endTime. `writeControl timeStep` tests writeTime_ = !(timeIndex_ % label(writeInterval_)) (OpenFOAM-v2606 Time.C:1114) and timeIndex_ is the GLOBAL time index, which does NOT reset across a `startFrom latestTime` restart: leg A had advanced it to 40, so writeInterval 400 fired at global index 400 = LEG-B STEP 360, t = 36.8, and the run directory carries 36.8/ and no 40.8/. R2 registers `writeControl runTime; writeInterval 111;` with endTime 111.8. runTime computes writeIndex = label(((value() - startTime_) + 0.5*deltaT_) / writeInterval_) and writes iff writeIndex > writeTimeIndex_ (Time.C:1117-1131), with writeTimeIndex_ initialised to 0 (TimeState.C:38) and startTime_ set to the restart time by `startFrom latestTime` (Time.C:180-183) -- so the index is RELATIVE TO THE RESTART and INDEPENDENT OF LEG A'S STEP COUNT ENTIRELY, and the + 0.5*deltaT_ term makes it robust to accumulated float drift in value(). THE ALTERNATIVE WAS REJECTED, NOT OVERLOOKED: keeping timeStep with writeInterval 1150 (= N_A + N_B) would also write once, but ONLY by arithmetic coincidence with leg A's step count -- the exact quantity that caused the defect -- so changing leg A would move the write again, silently. A fix that still depends on what broke it is not a fix. VERIFIED AT FOUR LEVELS: the source quoted by file and line; the branch TRANSCRIBED AND STEPPED over the full 1110-step schedule by derive_t25R6cR2.py, whose selftest requires that runTime writes exactly once at endTime, that a mutated interval writes more than once, AND that the timeStep setting T25R6c actually used REPRODUCES THE OBSERVED FAILURE (a write at leg-B step 360 and none at 40.8); run_one_t25R6cR2.sh grepping the leg-B controlDict ON DISK for runTime / 111 / 111.8 and refusing (exit 86/87/85); and the run itself, as PREDICTION P-R2-6, measured by rule 4.
_ExecutionTime_is_cpu_time_not_wall_time: ESTABLISHED FROM THIS BUILD'S SOURCE AND ITS ABI, NOT ASSUMED FROM CONVENTION, because T25R6c's A1.2(a) rests on which it is. CHAIN: OpenFOAM-v2606 Time.H:533 comments 'the elapsed ExecutionTime (cpu-time)'; TimeIO.C:631 prints elapsedCpuTime(); cpuTimeFwd.H typedefs cpuTime = cpuTimePosix on this build; cpuTimePosix.C:40-47 computes ((a.tms_utime + a.tms_stime) - (b.tms_utime + b.tms_stime)) / sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK) with value_type::update() calling ::times(this). ABI DEMONSTRATED ON THIS BOX: a C program executing THAT EXACT EXPRESSION across a 3 s nanosleep followed by a 1 s busy-loop returns CPU 0.98 s against wall 4.00 s, _SC_CLK_TCK = 100. times(2) fills tms_utime/tms_stime for the CALLING PROCESS ONLY -- children go to tms_cutime/tms_cstime, which OpenFOAM never reads. SO ExecutionTime IS RANK 0'S OWN USER+SYSTEM CPU: not wall, and not a sum over ranks.
_what_that_changes_about_the_contention_: IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE WITNESS THAT FIRED A1.2(a) DOES NOT SUPPORT ITS MECHANISM. A1.2(a) assumed a contended box INFLATES the measured rate; for the DESCHEDULING pathway that is BACKWARDS, since a descheduled process accrues LESS cpu-time. But the confound SURVIVES by two pathways cpu-time does not filter: memory-bandwidth and last-level-cache contention, which makes identical work cost more real cycles; and MPI busy-wait, where rank 0 SPINS in a collective while a descheduled peer catches up and the spin is charged to rank 0 as user cpu -- T25R6c measured ExecutionTime/ClockTime = 0.9573 (leg A) and 0.9921 (leg B), which is that signature. AND THE LOADAVG WITNESS: A1.2(a)'s breaking condition fired on /proc/loadavg 51.80 -> 52.96 -> 58.34 on 16 cores, but FIELD 4 OF THE SAME THREE WITNESSES READS 9/625, 9/625 AND 11/625 RUNNABLE. Linux loadavg is a 1-minute EWMA counting uninterruptible-sleep tasks alongside runnable ones, so it does NOT establish CPU oversubscription and 9-11 runnable against 16 cores does not either. run_one_t25R6cR2.sh now records nproc beside every loadavg witness so the ratio is never read without its denominator again. THE RESIDUAL CONFOUND IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: over T25R6c's settled leg-B steps the linear-solver iteration count is CONSTANT (92..94, a 2.150 % integer spread) while the 40-step window rate scatters by 2.915 % -- identical work, different cost, and that is the machine. R2 REGISTERS IN ADVANCE that a rho finer than about +/-3 % IS NOT ACHIEVABLE on this shared box at these window lengths. G-R2-2 is still readable because the predicted effect (rho - 1 = 7.52 %) is 2.58 floor-widths and the 1-sd band [1.0439, 1.1066] lies entirely above 1.0; a rho quoted to three decimals as a ceiling input is not readable, and that distinction is registered rather than discovered later. THE RANK MULTIPLIER IS AN ASSUMPTION AND IS NAMED AS ONE: core-min = ExecutionTime x 2 / 60 assumes rank 1 burns the same cpu as rank 0, and ExecutionTime cannot see rank 1. T25R6c used the same basis and R2 keeps it UNCHANGED so the two rungs stay comparable.
_why_the_legs_are_independent: r(leg A) and r(leg B) are means over DISJOINT sets of ExecutionTime deltas, parsed from TWO SEPARATE FILES written by TWO SEPARATE mpirun invocations, each starting its own ExecutionTime clock at zero. Neither number is computed from the other; no term appears in both but ranks and the constant 60, which cancel in the ratio. Nothing in the grader divides one leg's number by the other's to obtain a third and then offers the third back as corroboration. WHAT WOULD BREAK IT: (a) THE SHARED BOX -- MEASURED for the first time in this rung as R-R2-3, at constant solver work, and registered in advance as an irreducible ~3 % floor rather than witnessed and hoped about; (b) THE RESTART COUPLING -- which R2 both EXCLUDES (the first 40 leg-B steps are discarded) and CONTROLS (C-R2-1 measures the run's own transient end and refuses if it runs past 40), where T25R6c only caught it after the fact; (c) THE SHARED PARSER -- one instrument reads both legs and its defects cancel in the ratio only if multiplicative and identical across them, so the planted-zero control is planted into BOTH leg logs and read back AT THE PLANTED STEP in each.
_default_deny_order: 1 planted-zero control on the ExecutionTime reader, BOTH legs (rule 3) -- failure is a REFUSAL, exit 2, and issues NO verdict at all; 2 rule 4 completion, all conjuncts, both legs, AGE GUARD vs 0/module/T -- failure is NOT A RESULT, exit 4; 3 C-R2-1, the run's OWN transient must end at or before leg-B step 40 -- failure is NOT A RESULT, exit 4; 4 G-R2-1 PLATEAU, evaluated BEFORE rho is consulted -- failure is NOT A RESULT with rho printed beside it and NOT graded; 5 G-R2-2 DIRECTION -- rho < 1.0 is PASS, rho >= 1.0 is GATE FAIL. THE COMPARATOR REFUSES RATHER THAN DEGRADES.
